recipes.name: Mamacita's Mexican Rice
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste
0.25 cup frozen peas and carrots, thawed

steps.text: Cook and stir rice and oil in a skillet over medium heat until lightly toasted, about 2 minutes. Add onion and cook for 2 minutes. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Pour chicken broth into rice mixture and bring to a boil; stir tomato, cumin, saffron, salt, and black pepper into broth and bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer until rice is cooked, about 20 minutes.
Stir peas and carrots into cooked rice; garnish with cilantro.

raw_recipe.headline: Mamacita's Mexican Rice
raw_recipe.description: This quick and easy Mexican rice dish pan-fries white rice, onion, and garlic followed by simmering with chicken broth and tomatoes for a Mexican-inspired side dish.

review.reviewBody: I’m so pleased to have come across this untried recipe and be the first not only to review it, but to rate it highly. This is a winner. It’s rich, flavorful and colorful, not to mention just plain interesting. A LOT more interesting, in fact, than the typical tomato-based Mexican rice. I stayed true to the recipe save for the carrots, which I only omitted because I don’t care for them. Saffron, the most expensive spice as I know of, has a unique and characteristic flavor and color that really can’t be duplicated, tho’ turmeric would work as a more economical substitute. I made this to accompany Slow Cooker Guisado Verde and Skillet Summer Squash, both recipes also from this site. It was a beautiful and uncommonly delicious meal, in large part because of this beyond the ordinary Mexican rice. Mamacita, no doubt, is a darn fine cook. Thanks, Armi, for sharing her recipe.

We really like this. We have made this with cooked rice as well. When we do that we simply use 1 1/2 tsp Better Than Bullion in place of broth, and 3 TB tomato sauce in place of chopped tomatoes. It's otherwise identical. But, doing it with cooked rice means we can make a weeks' worth of rice, plain, at the beginning of the week, and season it any way we like as we go.
This was great. I didn't have the saffron, so I used a packet of Sazon Goya and I used an Instant Pot. It was moist and tasty.

I am so happy I came across this recipe! It is exactly what I've been searching for. This is how our Mexican restaurants here in AZ serve their rice. I love the light and fluffy texture and the flavors are perfection! I only added the peas, as I have picky carrot eaters. Next time I will add the roasted corn as one reviewer suggested. I did a pinch of my Saffron and a bit of Turmeric as well. I did all the steps through the last boiling and then poured it into my rice cooker. Came out perfect! I will definitely be making this again! For all that have bought Spanish Saffron at the store and paid $20+ for it. You can find it on Amazon as well much less. 2 grams/free shipping $11.95, that's the same size I saw at the store for $22. A little goes a long way for an amazing flavor.

EXCELLENT! I added the peas and carrots in w/ everything else, and used tumeric (Thanks, naples34102 for the idea!) in place of the saffron, b/c I didn't have any. Great flavor and super quick to make. I will def be using this recipe again and again~YUM! Thanks for sharing. :)

I'm adding this review to explain to people about the saffron. Mexican saffron sold in almost any store which carries Mexican products is very inexpensive. It is sold in dry form in a small packet or in jars almost like a thick salsa to add to food. I think in Spanish it is called "azafran". Not the expensive, imported stuff. This is a nice recipe. You can add tomato paste or sauce in place of the tomato. You can also omit the peas and carrots.

I think this recipe is wonderful! Prepares quickly and is delicious. I didn't like the idea of peas in my rice, so I added fire roasted corn. Also, I didn't have saffron so I used ground organic curry which consists of turmeric, cumin, red pepper and onion. I also added a shake or two of plain cumin. Plus, I didn't have any tomatoes, so I drained a can of diced ones and used half. The rice was a beautiful yellow and had fantastic flavor (I think the red pepper in the curry gave it a nice, spot on amount of heat!).

Great recipe as is with one step added. Begin by rinsing rice till water runs clear to remove excess starch. Then proceed as listed. Remember this dish was meant to compliment a spicy entree and should not be overly spiced itself. Thanks to Mamacita!

I made this as a side dish to tacos, and I really liked this recipe! I didn’t have any saffron, and decided to opt out of frozen veggies and instead used a fresh garden carrot that I diced and put in the dish at the same time as the tomatoes (I didn’t want crunchy carrots). I will make this dish again!

This was really tasty! I could have sworn I had saffron but after tearing the spice racks apart, I settled on some turmeric (from someone else's suggestion). I can't wait to try it again with saffron. I didn't have frozen peas and carrots so I diced up a big carrot and put it in the rice when it started to boil. Added the peas as directed. So good!
I threw everything into my rice cooker, and let it do its thing. Love my rice cooker!!!! Didn't need the vegetable oil, and I never add extra salt to anything.
One of our favorites! I make it again and again.
Great flavor. Definitely a keeper.
I made this and omitted the peas and carrots but add chopped yellow peppers. Definitely a winner!
The best Mexican Rice recipe around!
Moist and delicious

I think this is more of a Spanish Rice than. Mexican- thanks mostly to the saffron. As I added the peas and carrots, which are not in any Mexican rice dishes I’ve had before - reminded me of paella…and tasted similarly too. All that said; it is very good and pretty easy to make. Thanks Armi!

Made this rice as is only using all dried herbs and used crushed tomatoes instead. The flavor was wonderful. I had to add a bit more water to mine so the rice was fully cooked. I can totally see this rice as a side for Chicken Escabeche or Roscoe's Chicken both recipes from this site. WILL make it again in a heartbeat!
Winner for sure. Delicious rice recipe. I did make home made saffron to add to this recipe,
Didn't change a thing...so good, so quick. so easy and so tasty! Made this twice and it is in my permanent go-to recipe queue!
